- If sentiment is negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often over-optimistically extrapolates → cap forecast growth or introduce downward bias.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >10% from prior), model frequently overshoots → apply smoothing or reduce forecast slope for next 5–7 days.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to adjust → reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to ignore volatility → increase forecast volatility or add 1–2% buffer for downside risk.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections → adjust forecast downward by 3–8% in final 7–10 days if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ days), model tends to ignore it → reduce forecast by 1–3% per negative sentiment day.
